svg.aria-label: The problem leads the figure: available value does not reliably become realized value. Below it, where the product sits in the Blue Rewards system. The product is an enhanced experience inside the existing Blue Rewards app and website, nested within the programme systems of record, which are nested within BMO. The member is to the left, evidence authorities to the right, and forces outside the boundary across the top. Three feedback loops explain why realized value stays lower than it could be. B2, the proof and doubt brake, runs between the member and the evidence authorities. Five leverage points act on those loops, and the system feeds down into five downstream stakeholders.
svg.text: TEAM ZIG · BLUE REWARDS · SYSTEMS MAP
An enhanced experience within Blue Rewards
+ same direction · − opposite direction · ‖ significant delay · R reinforcing, B balancing
Available value does not reliably become realized value.
Members miss opportunities worth having, cannot tell what they are owed, and give up when value goes missing.
Realized value is the main variable. These three loops are why it stays lower than it could be:
should raise realized value — but its return leg is unconfirmed
caps realized value by limiting how generous offers can be
drains realized value by turning delay into withdrawal
• Existing earning methods: partner scans, linked-card offers, receipts, Shops and BMO products.
• Redemption fulfilment: gift cards, travel, merchandise and partner redemptions.
• BMO and partner support where manual investigation or partner action is required.
• Partner issuance, redemption and reversal: those services need partner credentials, not a member session.
privacy law, consent rules, suitability, disclosure
PC Optimum, Scene, bank and card ecosystems
formed by every other app they use, and not always realistic
a member, a BMO client, or both
what the enhancement is built around
What the programme records is what
a member did inside it, not everything
Owns Blue Rewards and funds it. Emerging Business, in gold, is our client.

The loyalty programme itself: the offers, the points, the catalogue, and the people who resolve cases.
We would read from these services and write back to them. We would not replace any of them.

One minus and a delay. The lag before a member can confirm that a purchase counted,
or that a missing reward is being handled, is what manufactures doubt.
Who this reaches, and what it would mean for them
Fewer missed earning and redemption opportunities, less searching,
a clear view of what is owed, and a way to recover what goes missing

Not issued value, activity or breakage. Changes the scoreboard, so it changes B1.
Make earned, pending, posted and used visible as one thing. Shortens the delay in B2.
Find at-risk value early and route it. This is the recovery capability.
Intrusion spends it. Personalization has a ceiling, capping how hard R1 is pushed.
Feed what actually arrived back into relevance. This is the return leg of R1.
